crime_highlights: Rakeem Anderson was stopped by police at a random motor vehicle checkpoint on Highway 102
A pat-down search located a loaded .22 calibre revolver in his waist band.
Mr. Anderson was arrested and charged with a number of firearms-related offences.
this is a highly dangerous situation
rationale_highlights: Mr. Anderson’s background and experiences provide a window into the lives of many African Nova Scotians who appear before the courts to be sentenced.
Even where the offence is very serious, consideration must be given to the impact of systemic racism and its effects on the offender.
The moral culpability of an African Nova Scotian offender has to be assessed in the context of historic factors and systemic racism, as was done in this case.
The African Nova Scotian offender’s background and social context may have a mitigating effect on moral blameworthiness.

Sentencing judges should take into account the impact that social and economic deprivation, historical disadvantage, diminished and non-existent opportunities, and restricted options may have had on the offender’s moral responsibility.
note: Crime narrative is thin; no victim harm in facts
